name: Python
tagline: A readable language for data analysis, automation and backend development
description: Python reads almost like English, which makes it easy to start with. It is used for automation scripts, neural networks, websites with Django and Flask, and data analysis with pandas.

name: JavaScript
tagline: The language of the browser and full-stack web development
description: JavaScript brings pages to life: it reacts to clicks, loads data without reloading and draws interfaces. With Node.js it also runs on the server, while React, Vue and Angular made it the main frontend language.

name: C++
tagline: Speed and memory control for games, engines and systems
description: C++ gives the programmer manual memory management and high performance. It is chosen for game engines (Unreal Engine), graphics, embedded systems, finance and scientific computing.

name: Java
tagline: The industry standard for backend development and Android
description: Java runs on the JVM, so the same code runs on Windows, Linux and macOS. It powers enterprise systems, banking backends, Spring services and Android apps.

name: C#
tagline: The .NET ecosystem language: Unity games, websites and desktop apps
description: C# combines Java's rigor with modern syntax. It is the main language for Unity games, ASP.NET for websites and WPF for desktop programs. Cross-platform .NET runs on all popular operating systems.

name: C
tagline: The foundation of operating systems and embedded devices
description: C is a minimalist language used to write the Linux and Windows kernels, drivers and firmware. It teaches you to understand memory, pointers and how things work under the hood.

name: Go
tagline: A simple and fast language for servers and microservices
description: Go was created at Google for convenient network service development. It has simple syntax, built-in concurrency with goroutines and fast compilation into a single binary. Docker, Kubernetes and high-load APIs are written in Go.

name: Rust
tagline: Memory safety without a garbage collector
description: Rust offers C++-level speed while checking memory safety at compile time. It is used in systems programming, WebAssembly, engines and network services.

name: PHP
tagline: A practical language for websites and server-side logic
description: PHP runs on the server and generates HTML. WordPress, Drupal and many online stores run on it. Modern PHP 8 means strict types, Composer and frameworks like Laravel and Symfony.

name: Kotlin
tagline: A modern language for Android and the JVM
description: Kotlin is compatible with Java but shorter and safer: less boilerplate, and null safety catches errors at compile time. Google recommends it as the primary language for Android.

name: Swift
tagline: The native language for iOS and macOS apps
description: Swift was created by Apple for development on its platforms. It is fast, safe and expressive, and SwiftUI lets you describe interfaces declaratively. You can't build iPhone apps without it.

name: TypeScript
tagline: JavaScript with static types for large projects
description: TypeScript extends JavaScript with types and compiles back to JS. It catches typos and data mismatches before runtime, which is why large frontend and backend projects use it with React, Angular and Node.js.

name: Ruby
tagline: An elegant language for rapid web application development
description: Ruby is valued for its beautiful, concise code. The Ruby on Rails framework lets you quickly build a full website: routes, database and admin panel. Ruby is also used for scripts and DevOps tools.

name: SQL
tagline: The database query language that no backend can live without
description: SQL does not replace a programming language but complements it: it describes which data to fetch or change. Knowing it is essential for working with PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite and analytics.

name: HTML/CSS
tagline: The foundation of any web page: structure and presentation
description: HTML defines the structure of a page, and CSS defines its appearance. They are not programming languages in the strict sense, but no website exists without them, so they come first on any web path.
